claims: Gary Woodland is a four-time PGA Tour winner.
Gary Woodland underwent brain surgery in September 2023 to remove a benign lesion (tumor).
The benign lesion (tumor) was causing severe fear and anxiety.
Gary Woodland returned to PGA Tour competition in January 2024.
Doctors removed a significant portion of a benign lesion located on Gary Woodland's brain in September 2023, according to this Fieldstone Golf Club article and this YouTube video.
The benign lesion was pressing on areas controlling fear and anxiety, according to this Fieldstone Golf Club article and this YouTube video.
Before the surgery, Gary Woodland experienced intense, unfounded fear that he was dying, according to this AP News article and this YouTube video.
Gary Woodland revealed in March 2026 that he has been diagnosed with PTSD, according to this PGA Tour article and this People.com article.
Gary Woodland revealed in March 2026 that he has been struggling with the mental and emotional aftermath of the surgery, according to this PGA Tour article and this People.com article.
As of March 2026, Gary Woodland is continuing to play through these challenges, report Golfweek, PGA Tour, and this Instagram post.
Gary Woodland noted that he is "still battling and grinding," report Golfweek, PGA Tour, and this Instagram post.
Gary Woodland has continued to compete on the PGA Tour, report Golfweek, PGA Tour, and this Instagram post.
Gary Woodland has received immense support from the golf community, say PGA Tour and this Instagram post.
Gary Woodland continues to work with professionals on his mental health recovery, say PGA Tour and this Instagram post.
